body:
## What happens

PR #2730 fixed #2599: `EditOperationParams` now moves a tilt with `basis_version` 0 to basis 1 when the A or B angle changes.

A project file can hold the defect already. The sequence is:

1. A build before the tilt basis change saved the project. Its tilts have no `basis_version` key, so they load as basis 0.
2. A build with defect #2599 opened the project. The user changed a tilt angle, for example to A0 B180 or A180.
3. That build saved the project with `basis_version: 0` and the new angles.

A build with the fix opens this file and keeps basis 0, because no angle changes in that session. The operation posts with the cut plane turned, as in #2599.

## Source

The read-only second review of PR #2730 found this group of files. The review did not build and did not make such a file. The decision entry `docs/decisions/2599-a180-legacy-basis.md` does not name this group.

## What is not known

- Whether a file can show that it has this state. A basis 0 tilt that was not edited is legal and must keep its output.
- Whether the preview and the post agree for such a file. The review says that they agree, from a reading of the code only.

## What should happen

Decide one of these and record the decision:

- The application finds such a file at load and tells the user, if a safe test exists.
- The release notes name the limit and the manual repair: change the tilt angle and change it back.

Do not migrate all basis 0 tilts at load. That changes the output of legal old projects.

Refs #2599

title: Research: dynamic test impact analysis for post-merge gates - coverage map + failure history to run likely failures first

body:
**Research only** (AGENTS.md "needs-research"): answer the questions, then file concrete sub-issues.

## Why
A post-merge gate should **fail fast**: the tests most likely to break after a merge should run first, so a red main is known in minutes, not after ~54 min. Today the order is fixed, and the only change-aware selection is the quick tier's hand-written gate maps (`Gate map (M4.4): covers ...`).

Motivating case (2026-11-19): PR #2664 changed the STEP importer and turned two suites red that its gate maps did not name: `camcraft-app feature_edge_g1_join` and `camcraft-kernel step_agreement` (#2713). Both were found only by the full post-merge run.

## Idea (dynamic, from the code and history - not hand maps)
1. **Coverage map:** after each green full run (or nightly), run the suites under coverage (`cargo llvm-cov`, per test) and store a map: test -> files/functions it executed. On a merge, the tests that executed the changed lines run first. (Here: `step_agreement` executes the STEP importer, so it would have ranked first.)
2. **Failure history:** record, per gate run, which tests failed and which files changed. Rank tests by P(fail | changed files) / duration; boost recent failures and new tests.
3. **Graph fallback:** the repo's graphify graph (`graphify affected`) for test -> code wiring when no coverage data exists for a file.
4. **Execution:** feed the ranked list to a parallel runner (nextest or the release-queue lanes, #2727), which starts each test as soon as its binary is built. The FULL suite still runs; ranking only changes the ORDER (the map can be wrong; a skip must never hide a failure).

## Open questions
1. Cost and stability of a per-test coverage run for the whole workspace (time on a 16-32 vCPU box; size of the map; how often to refresh it).
2. Granularity: file, function or line; how renames and moved code keep their history.
3. How the ranking reaches the gate (an input file to `xtask`, or a nextest filter/order).
4. Where the history lives (a file in the repo, a gate artifact, the post-merge workflow's cache).
5. Measured value: replay recent red post-merge runs and report time-to-first-failure with and without ranking.

## Measurements so far (#2727)
Same green commit 3a240b7fb: post-merge gate 53.4 min (warm, steps one at a time; 731 of 898 steps <= 1 s); `cargo nextest run` over the same scope 18.8 min cold on 16 vCPU, 8465 tests passed.

Done means: the questions are answered in comments, the sub-issues are filed (each with a P*, effort, area, Done-means, "Part of #this"), and this umbrella is closed.

Related: #2727, #2556, #2557, #2713.

body:
Found in the review of PR #2705 (issue #2561). The PR body of PR #2705 also names it.

What happens:
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs` (about line 193 on the PR branch) calls `contour_start::lead_held(p, poly[0], &lead)` for the first keep when the user picked a start point.
- On a tabbed level, `tab_bridge::moved_start` can move the first keep past the pick, because the first tab grows over the picked point. Then `poly[0]` is not the picked point.
- If no lead-in fits at the moved point, `lead_held` refuses the program. The message says `start point (x, y): no lead-in fits ...` with the moved point, not the point that the user picked.
- The automatic seam law does not refuse a point that is not picked. Thus a legal program can be refused, and the message names a point that the user did not pick.

This is not a silent wrong output. The result is a refusal or a misleading message.

Not proven by a test. The review read the code only.

Expected:
- Apply `lead_held` only when the first keep starts at the picked point.
- When the start moved, use the lead law of a keep that starts after a tab, and keep the `tabs:` note that names the move.

Done means: a test with a picked start that the first tab covers and a lead-in that does not fit at the moved point. The test shows that the program is not refused with the wrong point, or that the refusal names the correct point and the cause.

body:
**What happens:** `cargo xtask gate batch` (and every gate built on it: merge trains, post-merge checks) runs its ~620 steps strictly one after another (`xtask/src/exec.rs`, "the one-at-a-time loop"). Each step compiles and links one test binary, then runs it. Linking a large Rust test binary uses about one core.

**Evidence (2026-11-19, merge train on a 16-core Hetzner ccx43, main 409c0b5ab + one PR):**
- 1 h 20 min wall time; load average 2.7-2.8 on 16 cores for most of the run; the provider's CPU graph sits at ~100-300 % of 1600 %.
- At the moment checked: step 623 (`app suites: pocket3d_reach`), one `rustc` at 100 %, nothing else busy.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16` was set; it scales `-j` and `--test-threads` inside a step, but the steps themselves do not overlap.

The release tier already has parallel lanes (#2057, the longest-first queue of #2461), which took the release gate from 114.6 to 52.7 min. The batch tier does not use them.

**Proposal (two parts, either helps):**
1. **One parallel prebuild:** before the steps, build every test binary the plan needs in one cargo call (`cargo test --no-run -j N` over the planned packages/targets, with the same profile and features the steps use, so the steps reuse the artifacts instead of relinking one by one).
2. **Lanes for batch:** run the batch steps through the release queue's lanes (longest first, sharing the job budget), so several test binaries run at once.

Keep what the gate guarantees today: every step still runs and is logged, a red step still fails the gate, VOID detection is unchanged.

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate batch` on a 16-core host uses most of its cores during the build phase, and its wall time drops substantially against the same commit (measure before/after on the same machine; numbers in the PR).

Related: #2461, #2057, #2556, #2557.

title: Machine travel check refuses large-radius arcs: it judges the quarter points of the full circle, not the swept arc

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour around a part of about 1128 x 822 mm does not post. The machine check reports 40+ travel problems. The part, the stock and the work offset (G54) are correct.

```
post blocked - machine grblHAL 3-axis: 40 limit problem(s):
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches 21864.484 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -21346.099 in Y, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -22475.758 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -43516.220 in Y, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 32 reaches 14585.152 in X, ...
... (+284 more)
```

A larger machine does not help. The reported values grow with the arc radius, not with the part.

## Expected

The check judges the points that the arc really passes through. This program stays inside a stroke of -3000..3000, so it posts.

## Evidence

The part's long sides are gentle curves. The 2D Contour cuts them as arcs with very large radii. Values are relative to G54, read from the saved toolpath:

| Move | Radius | Sweep | Chord | Quarter point X+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | 22170 mm | 0.259 deg | 100.4 mm | 21864.484 |
| 32 | 14740 mm | 0.390 deg | 100.5 mm | 14585.152 |
| 33 | 11037 mm | 0.522 deg | 100.5 mm | 10981.565 |
| 34 | 8814 mm | 0.653 deg | 100.5 mm | 8839.776 |

The quarter point X+ of move 31 is exactly the value in the refusal (21864.484).

| Extent from G54 | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| Real cut (endpoints + quarter points inside the sweep) | -4.0 .. 1128.0 | -4.1 .. 821.5 |
| What the check uses (all four quarter points) | -22475.8 .. 21864.5 | -43516.2 .. 44333.6 |

## Cause

`crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs` `move_extremes` adds all four quarter points of the arc's full circle, also when the arc does not sweep through them. The doc comment says this is on purpose ("can only over-report"). That is harmless for small arcs. For a large-radius arc it refuses a legal program on every machine size.

The same function is used by the mill stroke check (`machine/mod.rs`) and by `plasma.rs`, `waterjet.rs`, `wire_edm.rs` and `lathe_stroke.rs`.

## Proposed fix

Add a quarter point only when the arc's sweep passes it. Use the start angle, the end angle and `arc.ccw`. A full circle keeps all four quarter points. Count a quarter point that lies on an endpoint. `crates/geometry/src/sketch_data.rs` `bounds` already does this for DXF arcs.

The sweep direction is the same `ccw` that the post writes as G2/G3. Thus the check stays exact and does not hide a violation.

## How to reproduce

1. Mount a 3-axis machine (I used grblHAL 3-axis, with the X/Y travel set to -3000..3000).
2. Import a part whose outline has long, shallow curves (here: a STEP model of 1128 x 822 mm).
3. Put G54 on the part corner and fit the stock.
4. Add a 2D Contour with an 8 mm end mill (EM-0800-4FL). Generate.
5. Post. The post is refused with the travel problems above.

I can share the project file (`.camproj`) privately.

## Related

- #2585 moves `judge.rs` to `camcraft-post`. Its output must not change, so this fix is separate. The second to land rebases.
- #1882 reads `move_extremes` for program bounds and has the same over-reach.

## Done means

- A large-radius arc with a short sweep inside the stroke does not give a travel problem.
- An arc that sweeps past a quarter point outside the stroke still gives a travel problem.
- The same arc in the other direction is judged on its own side.
- A full circle keeps all four quarter points.
- The existing stroke suites stay green (`vmc_stroke`, `machine`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_thread_travel`, plasma, waterjet, wire).

Suggested labels (for a maintainer): `bug`, `P3` (a legal program is refused), `effort:high` (safety floor: a travel check), `area:machine`.

body:
**Research only.** No code until the open questions are answered and the concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Where this comes from

Alex (@alextreseder; CamCraft Discord, 2026-11-19), who already helps with XYUV wire paths in #2690, is building a DIY EDM with the **G-EDM** spark generator and motion control. We may need a CamCraft post and machine file for it.

## What is public about G-EDM (from its project pages)

- Firmware **G-RBLv3** (github.com/G-EDM/G-RBLv3): a fork of Grbl (via Grbl_Esp32) reduced to a module inside the G-EDM code, for wire and sinker EDM machines on the G-EDM EVO / Gapstorm electronics.
- **Wire EDM runs from G-code files.** **Sinker EDM does not:** the firmware makes the sinker motion itself.
- The developer explains why stock Grbl/Marlin/LinuxCNC fit EDM poorly: the gap must be servo-controlled, and a feed hold can overrun the short-to-spark gap.
- **Licence:** the repository says its files are for private use only unless declared otherwise; commercial use and redistribution are prohibited. It is source-available, not open source.

## Clean-room and licence limits

- We use the **public behaviour and documentation** only (which G-code words the firmware reads, units, arcs, the meaning of feed), and the owner's own observations. We **do not copy or derive code** from G-RBLv3 (its licence forbids it, and the clean-room rule applies to everything we ship).
- No material from Autodesk products.

## Open questions

1. Which G-code subset does G-RBLv3 accept for wire EDM: units, absolute/incremental, G2/G3 arcs (I/J or R), G41/G42 or pre-offset paths only, comments, program start/end?
2. Is it 2-axis (XY) only, or does it support U/V (taper / XYUV, which ties to #2690)?
3. What does F mean on an EDM gap-servo machine: a maximum feed, or ignored? Which M-codes switch the spark, flushing, wire feed and tension, if any?
4. Can CamCraft's existing wire path (Wire Contour, kerf offset, skims) map onto it, or is a different structure needed (e.g. one pass, the firmware sets the conditions)?
5. Is sinker EDM in scope at all, given that the firmware makes the sinker motion itself (maybe only a setup/position export)?
6. What machine-file data do we need (travels, wire diameter, guide heights)?

## What would help (from Alex)

- Which G-EDM electronics and firmware version he runs, and whether his build is wire, sinker or both.
- A short wire program that his G-EDM accepts (any simple shape), and anything the firmware refuses.
- Later: a dry run of a CamCraft test program, no cutting needed.

Related: #2690 (XYUV swallowtails), #617 (Sodick wire post), the existing `wire-iso` post.

## Done means

The questions above are answered in comments, and the concrete sub-issues (post, machine file, refusals) are filed, each with one P*, one effort label, area labels, a Done-means line and "Part of #this"; then this umbrella is closed.

- Add integration tests in `crates/app/tests/` running generation through `sim::verify::wire` (`kerf`, `threading`, and `slug` laws) to verify healed cuts never gouge or drop the wrong slug.

body:
Sew XYUV rulings consistently across planes when one plane heals a swallowtail and the other plane does not.

## Context

When XY trims a tight corner fillet or bridges a shallow slot, its offset ring `wu`/`wl` loses arc length while UV keeps the full arc. Pairing directly by trimmed offset arc length (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/pairing.rs`) shifts rulings out of phase around the contour and can trigger `folds`, `crossing`, or `too_far`. Also, `ruled_widen::away` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_widen.rs`) computes widening directions from unhealed `given` edges, which can reverse steps near a trimmed vertex.

## What this does

- Build a monotone preimage map from each healed offset ring's edge midpoints and vertices back to arc positions on its original input profile `given`.
- Collapse any excised input span `(s_a, s_b)` to the corresponding trimmed intersection vertex `V_trim` so `ArcLength` and `SyncPoints` pairings generate clean cone/fan rulings from `V_trim` to the opposing plane (`pairing.rs` and `ruled.rs`).
- Snap sync points that fall inside an excised corner span directly to `V_trim` instead of shifting across adjacent flanks.
- Update `ruled_widen::away` to derive the outward miter/offset direction from the surviving offset ring segments at trimmed vertices so per-ruling widening does not reverse or tangle.
- Verify all ruled-surface laws (`folds`, `crossing`, `lean_law`, and 33-height `clearance` against the unhealed `product` surface) on the sewn rulings.

## Done means:

- Asymmetric XY/UV shapes (for example a sharp inside corner or tight fillet on XY paired with an open fillet on UV) generate clean fan rulings without phase drift, false folds, or widening reversals.
- `clearance` catches mid-height wall gouges from bridging across a deep slot on one plane and refuses them by name.

body:
**Research only.** No code until the open questions below are answered and the concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Where this comes from

A wire EDM user, Alex (@alextreseder; CamCraft Discord, 2026-11-19), asked whether our XYUV (+Z) path is collision-aware and handles swallowtails. His points, in short:

- The easy case: the wire (kerf) radius is smaller than every local radius of the part. Then each ruled face is offset with an arc join and projected onto the XY and UV planes.
- The hard case: the radius is not smaller than all local radii. Then the degenerate **local and global swallowtails** must be healed and sewn with a bounded-tolerance technique. In general this is one of the hardest CAD-kernel problems, but for wire EDM it splits into **two 2D problems** (the XY and UV planes), which makes it tractable.
- He has a working procedure (currently a FreeCAD macro) and offered to share it.

## What CamCraft does today (main)

- 4-axis ruled wire cut (#537): an upper and a lower closed profile, paired into rulings by normalised arc length or by sync points (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs`, `pairing.rs`); per-ruling widening (#1170, `ruled_widen.rs`).
- Kerf: each profile is offset in 2D, and the rulings are laid over those parallels.
- Degenerate results are **refused, not healed**: the fold law (the ruled surface folds back between rulings) and the crossing law (the surface crosses itself at the quarter heights) in `ruled_laws.rs`, plus the kerf and gouge laws, run before the path leaves the generator.

So the easy case works, and the hard case gives a refusal with a reason. Healing is the gap.

## Open questions

1. Which swallowtail cases occur in practice for XYUV: local (one corner tighter than the kerf radius) and global (two distant parts of a profile approach each other), on the XY plane, the UV plane, or both, and when the two planes disagree?
2. What is the healing procedure? Trim the self-intersections of each 2D offset (published offset-curve methods), then re-pair the rulings? How is the pairing kept consistent when one plane loses a loop the other plane keeps?
3. What tolerance bounds the healing, and how is the result checked (the fold and crossing laws must still pass on the healed surface)?
4. When healing changes the cut part (a corner the wire cannot reach), how is that shown to the user: the existing uncut-corner note, or a refusal when the change is above a tolerance?
5. Which of today's refusals would become healed results, and which must stay refusals (Prime Directive: correct or visibly refused)?

## What would help (from Alex or anyone)

- A **written description** of the procedure: steps, tolerances, how local vs. global swallowtails are sewn.
- If the macro itself is shared: its **licence**. We can reuse code only under a licence compatible with this project (MIT or Apache-2.0); otherwise we implement from the description and from published literature.
- **Test shapes** that make local and global swallowtails (simple STEP or DXF profiles, upper and lower). These become test fixtures for the fold and crossing laws even before any healing exists.

Clean-room: published literature, the contributor's own description, and our own design notes only; no material from Autodesk products.

## Done means

The questions above are answered in comments, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one P*, one effort label, area labels, a Done-means line and "Part of #this"); then this umbrella is closed.

body:
## What Happens

`ImportModel::within` (crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs, #2463) reads and parses the file, then reads the file a second time for its SHA-256. If the file changes between the two reads, the model holds the first bytes and the link records the second digest. The link check then sees no change. That change is never imported.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Link a model to a file, or import the file.
2. Change the file while the import parses it (a large model, one save during the parse).
3. The model keeps the old geometry. Its operations do not go Stale. The status line says nothing.

## Workaround

Save or touch the file once more. The digest differs from the recorded one, and the check imports the file again.

## What Should Happen

Read the file once. Take the digest from the bytes that the parse used. `ImportModel::graded` already takes bytes in hand; use the same path for a file import.

## Source

Found in the review of PR #2563 (head `aef4f610c`), 2026-11-19. The code comment in `within` names the window. The window is one parse time.

Filed by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-19): "I want to be able to type text, select a face and location for the text, text size and a tool and it does the engraving. It's common for people to want engraved part numbers but it isn't modeled."

## What the user wants

1. Type a text string, for example a part number `SN-0471`.
2. Pick the face to engrave and place the text on that face.
3. Set the text height and the tool.
4. CamCraft makes the engraving toolpath, verifies it and posts it.

## What exists today

- `OpType::Engrave` and `OpType::Trace` machine 2D geometry along the tool centreline. They obey the mark law (#1595): a shallow mark passes, a deep cut is refused.
- 2D geometry comes from a DXF sketch (the `Sketch` entity, #1862). Work to feed sketch chains to Engrave and Trace is #1869. SVG import is #1880.
- There is no way to make geometry by typing text. A user today must draw the letters in a CAD program, export a DXF, and import it.

## What to build

- A text-to-outline step: convert the typed string into glyph outlines as 2D regions (outer loop + hole loops for letters such as A, B, O). Use one of the fonts already bundled in `assets/ui/fonts/`; the outlines are the same vectors the UI draws. Flatten the glyph curves to polylines within the setup tolerance. Clean-room: only the font's own licensed outlines, no vendor letter shapes.
- An undoable command (for example `InsertText`): the text string, height, and the placement become a `Sketch` the operation kinds already read. Ship its MCP tool with it (#128 law).
- Placement: select a planar face (or the setup top plane) in the viewport, then set X/Y and rotation. The existing `sketch::face_frame` code gives the face frame.
- Parameters on the Engrave operation: text string, height (mm or inch through the unit lens), letter spacing, depth (bounded by the mark law), tool, feed, and climb. The toolpath path is the existing Engrave/Trace generator.
- Two ride modes later, both from the same outlines: ride the glyph boundary with a small end mill or v-bit, and single-line engraving on the glyph skeleton with a v-bit. Pick one for the first cut; record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.

## Suggested label triage

`enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: new toolpath and posted G-code). The filing account has no label rights; a collaborator sets these.

## Done means

The user types a string, picks a face and a spot, sets a height and a tool, and CamCraft generates, verifies and posts an engraving toolpath. A golden test pins the CL output for a known string and font. The placement, `.camproj` round-trip and MCP tests pass.

The finding is false. No part material stands above the cut plane at that rim. The outer rim of a Face is open: its rows cross the rim by design.

## Expected

No finding for a Face move whose end is near an open rim. A move near a wall (part material above the cut plane) is still reported.

## Repro

- Part: a plate 40 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10). One dia 6 through-hole at (-12, 0).
- Stock: a box 40 x 60 x 12 mm (z 0..12).
- Tool: `EM-1000-4FL` (dia 10).
- Operation: Face, source the part, `holes: lift` (the default), Cut Z fixed 10, stepover 4, clearance 30.

Result on upstream main 1ae4d061f with the fix of #2437 applied: 5 plunges, and `Gouge` findings at moves 15, 18, 27 and 30. Move 15 is the plunge at X -18.227 Y -5 after the lift. It is 1.77 mm inside the rim at X -20.

## Cause (found during #2437)

`sim::verify::section::tangency` reads each law point against all loops of `cx.region` with the distance floor `r - tol`. In `Mode::Boundary` with a model, it does not ask if the region edge is a wall. `wall_gouge` in the same file has that classification for the whole-move reading (a region edge is a wall when the model section holds a probe beside the edge midpoint).

## Workaround

Use `holes: through` or `holes: cut_air` when the holes are air, or use a stock source.

## Notes

- This is a change to a gouge law. It needs a pin that a wall below the model top is still reported.
- #2437 removed the lifts for holes below the cut plane. This defect stays for holes at the cut plane.

**Done means:** a Face that lifts over a hole near the open outer rim has no finding; a test pins it, and a second test pins that a move within a tool radius of a wall is still reported.

**Scope** (his suggestion): 2 passes first - entry `C000`, rough `C001`, sizing `C002`. Polishing (`C903+`) later.

**Open questions for the reporter** (asked on #617): where in the program each C word goes (on the threading/entry move, at each pass start); whether `C000` is used for every start hole; an example program from an LN control (his earlier AQ600L example on #617 shows a condition table in the header).

Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 1 of 5.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The ball drop-cutter of 3D finishing tests every facet for each sample. `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` lines 368-388) loops over all `Sup` entries with a padded box reject only. Each accepted candidate calls `ball_clear` (lines 132-142), which loops over all facets again. `column_clear` (line 162) does the same. There is no spatial index. The cost is about samples x facets.

The GPU filter of #2526 must match a CPU reference. This slice makes that reference: a CPU grid of facets that the GPU result is tested against. It is also the largest speed gain (estimate in #2526, comment 3/4).

## What
- Bin the `Sup` entries (from `build_sups`, lines 27-50) into a uniform XY grid by their padded box (`xmin..xmax`, `ymin..ymax`, already padded by `r`).
- `support_at`, `ball_clear`, `column_clear` and the fold scan (`edge.rs` `fold_best`) read only the facets of the cells that the query touches.
- The same f64 functions run. The subset must hold every facet whose padded box contains the query point. This keeps the result the same bits.
- Optional, same PR or a follow-up: run the raster lines in parallel with an order-preserving `collect`.
- No GPU code in this slice.

## Prime Directive
- The grid is conservative: a facet goes into each cell that its padded box touches. A bin miss would let `ball_clear` pass a ball that touches a facet. A test pins the superset rule.
- Degenerate input (NaN box, zero-area facet, a box past the coordinate guard) goes to every cell or gives a clean `GenError`. It never panics.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- The 3D finishing goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/` give the same `.cl` and `.cnc` bytes as before.
- A new motion test: for random sample points over a fixture, the grid query answers the same `support_at` and `ball_clear` values as the full scan.
- A new motion test: each facet whose padded box contains a point is in the grid query of that point (superset law).

## Readings
Measure the time of one large 3D finishing operation before and after (release build). Put the numbers in the PR body.

## Decision entry
Not needed if the change stays inside `camcraft-motion`. No new crate edge, no new dependency.

Effort: `effort:high` by the safety floor (toolpath generation and its gouge certifier).

Done means: the 3D finishing support scan uses a facet grid, the goldens are byte-equal, the superset and parity tests pass, and the PR states the speed readings.

Part of #2525 (slice 1 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What to add

Add a CPU module in `camcraft-geometry` (for example `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster/`) that converts a `geo2d::Region` to a bit-packed grid of cells. This is the base of the raster nest of #2525. It has no GPU code and no wgpu.

- A grid has an origin, a cell size (integer, in `geo2d::SCALE` units) and a width and height in cells. Rows are packed in `u32` words.
- **Over-approximate mode** (for parts): mark each cell that the region touches. A cell that only touches the boundary is marked.
- **Under-approximate mode** (for the usable sheet): mark a cell free only when the full cell is inside the region. Holes of the region are not free.
- Use integer arithmetic on the `geo2d` integer coordinates only. No float enters the decision of a cell.
- Refuse by name: a non-positive cell size, a grid larger than a stated cell limit, a non-finite input, an empty region where one is required.
- One-line provenance comment: scanline polygon fill and conservative coverage, from Bennell and Oliveira (EJOR 2008) and general computer-graphics literature.

## Why

The raster finds nest positions fast. It is only a first filter. A raster "free" result must be a true "free" result: parts over-approximate, the sheet under-approximates (#2525, research comment 2).

## Notes

- No new crate edge, no new dependency, no decision entry for an edge. Record the cell-size default and the cell limit in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`.

## What happens

`onProbeResult` in `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps` (PR #2310) writes the found work offset as:

```
G10 L20 P<SetWorkOffset + 1> X[#5420-#<dev>] Y[#5421-#<dev+1>] ...
```

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` on `main` has the same pattern (`onProbeResult`, the `G10 L20` block with `#5420`).

One of these:

- The post makes the target WCS active (or proves it is active) before it reads `#5420`-`#5422`.
- The post refuses by name a `SetWorkOffset` that is not the WCS of the section.

## Evidence

- Review of PR #2310 (non-blocker 3).
- LinuxCNC G-code reference: `G10 L20` ("the current coordinates become the given values") and the parameters `#5420`-`#5428` (current position in the active coordinate system).

body:
## What happens

The bridge check in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_bridge.rs` came with PR #2486. It compares only two neighbouring cuts: the cut before a tab and the cut after it.

The check reads only the last `W + D` of the walk before the tab. It reads only the first `W + D` of the walk after the tab. Lead-in and lead-out moves are included.

A different cut can come closer than the tab width. The check does not read that cut. Two cases are known:

- A U-turn of the same ring. A later part of the ring comes near the tab.
- A different ring at the same level.

The reviewer of head `613ba4abf` says that the tab then holds through a strip that is narrower than W. Main had the same limit before PR #2486. The decision file `docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md` records this limit.

## Cases seen in the build review (not confirmed as tab necks)

- A 60 x 7 mm inside slot, W = 3 mm, 3 mm tabs. Two cut runs are 2.06 mm apart. The output has no note. The reviewer says the ring is almost a line here, so the distance is across the slot. The reviewer did not confirm a tab neck.
- An inside L-shape with Perpendicular, Arc or Tangential leads. Lead cuts on the two walls of a 14 mm arm come within 0.07 to 3.4 mm of each other. The cuts are in scrap material, far from the tabs. The reviewer says this was present before PR #2486 and is not a bridge failure.

## First step

Write a shape-mask test in `crates/motion/tests/common/shape_mask.rs` (see AGENTS.md, "2D toolpath shape-mask tests"). Use the U-turn case and the second-ring case. Measure the narrowest bridge.

- If no bridge is narrower than the tab width, post the result on this issue. Keep P3.
- If a bridge is narrower than the tab width, raise this issue to P1. AGENTS.md sets P1 for unsafe output.

## Smaller points

- [ ] `SLACK = 1e-6` (`tab_bridge.rs:77`) has no margin for arc chord error. The reviewer found no bridge under W in a probe, but says the margin is small.
- [ ] With a picked start, the windows grow backward only (`tab_bridge.rs:104`, `128-129`). If the first window grows past the pick, the first keep no longer starts at the pick. No note says this. `contour.rs:307-309` then checks `lead_held` on a keep that is not at the pick. The reviewer says this is not a gouge. Add a `tabs:` note, or a refusal by name.
- [ ] No test has more than one tabbed level. The tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs` use TAB_H = 1 and a stepdown of 2. The reviewer's probe with three levels gave a correct result. Add a test with more than one tabbed level.

## Done means

- The shape-mask result is posted on this issue.
- Each smaller point is fixed, or has a `tabs:` note or a named refusal, with a test that pins it.

Refs #2480
Found in the reviews of PR #2486.

body:
## Request

Add a post for Mach3 Mill (3-axis). Mach3 is still on many retrofit mills and routers. The `Mach4` post writes words and macros that Mach3 does not read in the same way.

## Differences to the Mach4 post

From the public "Using Mach3Mill" manual (behaviour only):

- Canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98` / `G99`. `G84` needs a tapping head setup: refuse a tap by name unless the machine file says that tapping is available.
- `G4 P` dwell: Mach3 reads P in seconds or in milliseconds by a setting ("G04 dwell param in ms"). The post must have an option for this. Default: seconds, as in the manual.
- Tool change: `T<n> M6`, then `G43 H<n>`. The `M6` behaviour depends on the user's `M6Start` / `M6End` macros, so the post does not assume a retract inside `M6`. It retracts first.
- Arcs: the IJ mode (absolute or incremental) is a Mach3 setting. The post must not depend on it: it writes the IJ mode word that the user selects in an option (default incremental IJ). The goldens must be checked against the manual for the word that Mach3 reads. A header comment names the mode.

## Request

Add a post for classic Grbl 1.1 (3-axis mill). Many small routers and hobby mills run Grbl 1.1 on an Arduino-class board. The `grblHAL` post (#710) writes words that Grbl 1.1 refuses, so it is not a replacement.

From the public Grbl 1.1 documentation (the "Commands" and "Interface" wiki pages, behaviour only):

- No canned cycles. Grbl 1.1 has `G80` but not `G73`, `G81`-`G89`. The post must expand drill, peck and bore cycles to `G0` / `G1` / `G4` moves.
- No `M6`. A tool change is `M5`, a retract to a safe Z in machine coordinates (`G53 G0 Z...`), then `M0` with a comment that names the tool. `T` is written in a comment only.
- No `G43 H`. The length offset is `G43.1 Z...` or nothing. Default: write no length offset (the user zeroes each tool), and write `G49` in the preamble.
- No `O` program number. No `G41` / `G42`. No `G98` / `G99`.
- `G4 P` is in seconds.
- Line buffer of 80 characters: keep each block short. Comments are `( )` only. Do not write comments with nested brackets.
- Coolant: `M7`, `M8`, `M9` only. Other coolant kinds are refused by name.

## Acceptance

- A built-in post `Grbl 1.1` and a machine file `grbl-3axis.mch`.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill (expanded), peck (expanded), bore with dwell, two tools.
- A test that each posted line is 80 characters or less, and that no unsupported word (`G8x`, `M6`, `G43 H`, `G41`, `G42`, `O`) is posted.

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, stacked on PR #2342).

**What happens.** Rotary Parallel lays the bar down and runs the finishing raster over the whole model, end faces included (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary.rs`, `rotary_parallel`). Each end face is finished down to the fitted axis. On rotary work the bar is held at one end (chuck) or both (chuck and centre), so the chuck-side "end face" of the model is inside solid bar. The pass there is a groove one tool diameter wide, cut from the skin to the centreline: it parts the bar.

**Evidence.** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` on the #1904 branch: a cylinder model 0.680 in across from X-1.25 to X0, a Box stock from X-2 to X0, a 1/8 in ball tool. The posted program (`examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`) feeds the tool tip at X-1.3125 down to Z-0.029 (Z is the radius from the A centreline), with the stock box going on to X-2. Pinned by `continuous_4axis_part::the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline`.

What stops it today, and what does not:
- A tool whose flute is shorter than the depth is blocked at post: "shank/holder at move N collides with the uncut stock" (pinned by `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`, 1/2 in flute). Good.
- A tool with a long enough flute (5/8 in here, or the catalog `BN-0600` default of 15 mm) posts with no warning.
- No setting keeps the pass off an end face. **Bottom Z** is a floor in the laid frame, not a radius: at 0 it keeps only the half of the bar within about 81 degrees of the top and still cuts the end faces to the axis. **Top Z** / **Clearance Z** are radii for the links. There is no axial window (Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset read heights as stations; on a bar lying flat those are inert).
- The kit golden of PR #2342 (`wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) has the same shape: its stock ends where its model ends, so CamCraft sees air where the real bar goes on into the jaws.

**Expected.** A way to finish the turned surface only: an axial window (from/to stations along the fitted axis), or an option to leave the end faces, so the pass stops at a shoulder. Until then, a named warning or refusal when an end-face pass enters stock that goes on past the end of the model.

**Workaround.** None for a real cut on a held bar. The #1904 guide page runs the program as an air cut only and says why.

Priority note: filed as P3 (wrong behaviour with no silent gouge of the part: the stock is cut, the model is not). The maintainer may read "parts the bar off with no warning" as P1.

Done means: a Rotary Parallel job on a bar that goes on past the model's chuck-side end either leaves that end face alone by a setting, or is refused or warned by name; a test pins it; the #1904 guide page drops its "air cut only" limit.

1. A post script declares its options in its own code: a key, a label, a type (boolean, integer, number, one of a list), a default, a group and a short description. Define this declaration format for our `.cps` files and document it.
2. The post engine (`camcraft-post`) reads the declared options of the selected post without a run of the program.

4. The user changes a value. The posted program uses the changed value. Examples: coolant flood or mist, the work offset word format of the control, sequence numbers on or off.
5. A changed value is stored with the project, for each setup or each program and each post. A change goes through an undoable command. The command has an MCP tool, and the CLI can set an option.
6. The engine validates each value against the declared type and range when the command is created. A value that the script does not declare is refused with a diagnostic.

8. Give the shipped post scripts their first options. Start with the options that the scripts now hold as fixed values.

- Where a setting is already a document or setup parameter (program units, the work offset slot, the coolant of a tool), the post option must not be a second source. The option changes only how the post writes the value. Name each such case in the decision file.

This is an umbrella issue. Research it, then file one sub-issue for each part, and close this issue.

## Parts

1. **Layout.** Put each label on the left of its input field, in a property grid (see the Fusion-style dialog rule: collapsible groups, tooltips).
2. **Cutting data by material is the default.** Each tool has cutting data (speed, feed, stepdown, stepover) for each material. The current single set of values becomes the data of a material named `Unknown`. `Unknown` is the default material. Existing tool libraries and project files load with their values moved to `Unknown`, with no loss.
3. **One preview.** The editor shows one drawing: the tool profile and the holder that the user selected. Remove the second preview. (See #2005: the body and the spun profile draw over each other.)
4. **Holders come from the holder library.** The user selects a holder from the library. The holder values (diameter, length, gauge length) come from the library entry and are not typed into each tool. Remove the parametric holder fields from the tool.
5. **A holder is not sized to a tool.** One holder entry (for example a Weldon holder) serves each tool whose shank fits it. Do not keep one holder entry for each tool size. The fit check (shank diameter against the holder bore) must give a clear refusal when a tool does not fit.

- The tool library and project file format change (parts 2, 4, 5). Give the migration and the version bump. This can be a breaking change.
- How the collision check and the simulation get the holder shape after part 4. They must use the same shape that the preview shows.

labels.name: enhancement

body:
What the user asked for (chat, 2026-11-14): "i want it to form a smooth link move over holes in the surface. lets start with a straight line between each edge of the hole. later we can add splines and curves for how to connect them."

What happens now: finish3d (Parallel and the other march patterns) breaks a raster line where the tool cannot stand, for example over a hole. The chain between the two runs lifts to the retract plane. The tool makes an air hop for every gap. On a part with many holes this is slow and the moves look wrong in the GUI.

Change: add an operation parameter `gap_link` to the finishing parameters. The parameter is a dropdown with two options:

- `Jump` (default): today's behaviour, unchanged. The chain lifts to the retract plane.
- `Straight`: one straight Feed move between the end of one run and the start of the next, at the two end points' own tip height.

Law for `Straight`: both run ends stand at tangent centers by the march construction. The author certifies the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS`. A grazing contact at the rim passes. A real bite refuses. On a refusal the chain takes the `Jump` hop. No air margin is added for `Straight`; `Jump` keeps its own retract law.

Also fixed, needed by this feature: the raster serpentine ran a broken back line wrong. It reversed only each piece's points and kept the pieces in grid order. Every gap link then jumped back across the field instead of crossing its gap. A back line now reverses whole: the pieces in reverse order, and each piece's points reversed. This also shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines.

How the parameter is stored: the project digest takes a `0x4D` tag plus a variant byte only when `gap_link` is not `Jump`. The project file grammar takes the words `jump` and `straight`. No project-file version step-up. The MCP params door and the UI combo carry the same two options.

Done means:

- The Gap link dropdown offers Jump and Straight; Jump is the default and writes the old bytes.
- Over a holed plate, `Straight` authors rim-to-rim Feed links at the run height and no retract hop for those gaps.
- A `Straight` link that would cut the part is refused, and the hop stands (Prime Directive).
- Every gap crossing on a broken back line spans one gap, never the field.
- Pins: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs`, the round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`, and the MCP params-door test.

Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP.

## What happens

The part is a 30 mm cube made of two L-shaped halves with 15 mm quadrant steps. Every edge, convex and concave, has an R3.125 mm fillet. The only cutter is a 1/4 in (6.35 mm) 3-flute **flat** end mill.

- **3D Finish takes only a ball nose** (`list_operation_types`: `"tool_kinds": ["BallNose"]`). With the flat end mill, the op is refused:

- There is no **z-level (waterline) finish** with a flat or bull-nose tool. That is the usual way to finish steep walls and convex fillets with the tool already in the spindle.

A finishing strategy that works with flat and bull-nose cutters:

- **z-level / waterline contours** on the model at a set stepdown (or scallop height), at least for steep regions;
- the tool's real shape (flat bottom, corner radius) used for the gouge offset;
- the shallow areas left to a later pass or flagged as rest.

A flat tool still cannot form a concave fillet smaller than its corner radius, and the rest check should say so. It can follow convex fillets and walls.

**Done means:** 3D Finish (or a new 3D Contour kind) accepts flat and bull-nose tools with a z-level pattern. On a filleted block with a flat end mill it generates gouge-free waterline passes at the set stepdown, and verify reports the concave-fillet rest. A pinning test covers the flat and bull-nose cases.

body:
> bug; tools like plasma cutter - or laser for that matter, and prob waterjet as well. Would require piercing and dwell data.. Lasers usually have 1-4 piercing steps that can be used all or just one. just to get thru different thickness of material. Same with plasma.. piercing height, power at height, pressure of gas, movement of torch/laser head etc etc. Use perplexit to research this in a subagent and make a issue ticket from it where this types of tools getter better coverage.

(Maintainer, 2026-11-13, in chat.)

## What exists today

- Plasma only. `ToolKind::Torch` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs`) is a kerf width plus rpm 0; it carries no cutting data. I found no laser or waterjet tool kind in `tools.rs`.
- The plasma operation (`crates/motion/src/plasma/mod.rs`, `emit.rs`; app side `crates/app/src/operation/types/plasma.rs`, `crates/app/src/project/plasma_dto.rs`; page `crates/ui/src/egui_app/plasma_page.rs`) has three optional per-operation numbers: pierce height, cut height, pierce delay. Left empty means "set by the controller" (AutoFS).
- The Tormach plasma post (`assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`) writes M207/M208/M209 for those three values and G16 for the pierce, and leaves volts, amps and gas to the control's own table. Nothing else (power, gas, pressure, torch motion at the pierce) can be stated anywhere.
- Related open issues: 621 (plasma research umbrella), 1447 (common-line cutting and marking), 1452 (DXF import for 2D cuts). No open issue covers pierce data; a "pierce" search finds only closed plasma work (670, 671).

## What is missing

1. Cut data lives on the operation, not on the tool, and is not keyed by material or thickness. Changing plate thickness means re-typing numbers.
2. Only one pierce, with one height and one delay. No transfer height, no puddle-jump (lift after pierce), no creep or start-speed ramp on exit, no amperage or gas on the tool.
3. Laser and waterjet have no tool kind, so there is nowhere to put multi-stage pierce data.
4. Posts have no way to say "this stage cannot be written in this dialect".

## Research summary (facts and concepts only, own words)

Plasma
- Transfer height: the low height where the arc first transfers to the plate. Pierce height: the higher height held while the arc pierces (limits spray onto the torch). Pierce delay: time held after transfer before the head moves. Cut height: stand-off while cutting. Torch height control holds a target arc voltage as a stand-in for the distance during the cut.
- Puddle jump (optional): after the pierce, lift to a percentage of pierce height for a short dwell to clear molten metal, then drop to cut height.
- Each system and consumable set has a maximum pierce thickness; thicker plate needs an edge start (the arc begins off the plate edge). Kerf comes from the cut chart.
- The maker's cut chart is the source of values (current, gas type and pressure, heights, voltage, speed). It normally sits in the control's material table; the program selects it and may override single values.

Laser
- Makers document up to four sequential pierce stages, each with its own time, power, pulse frequency, duty cycle, focus, nozzle distance, gas type and pressure; a stage with zero time is skipped. Parameters may ramp from a start to an end value inside a stage.
- Pierce kinds named by makers: ramped, pulsed (gradual), and a forceful short pierce; definitions vary by machine, so the data model must not hard-code them.
- Cooling dwell or gas blow is machine-specific; no standard length exists.
- Normal practice: the technology table (material and thickness) holds the recipe, the NC program selects the table and pierce type and may override.

Waterjet
- Methods: stationary, dynamic (moving toward the path while piercing), wiggle or circular (short oscillation), and low-pressure or pressure-ramp pierce for brittle or laminated material (glass, stone, ceramic, composites). Abrasive can be delayed after water starts, or fed first with pressure ramped up from low.
- No universal pierce time by thickness exists; it depends on material, pressure, nozzle and method, so it must be the user's value.

Control table versus program: recipes are usually in the control's table (selected by material and thickness) with the program choosing and sometimes overriding. A CAM system therefore needs both: store the recipe, then either post the selector or post explicit values, by dialect.

## Proposed data model

A cut-data record per tool, keyed by material and thickness (rows the user adds, copies and deletes):

- Cut parameters: cut height, feed, kerf; for plasma amperage, gas type and pressure, arc voltage; for laser power, frequency, duty, gas type and pressure, nozzle distance, focus; for waterjet pressure and abrasive flow.
- Pierce: an ordered list of 0 to 4 stages, every stage optional and individually enableable. Each stage has height, duration (dwell), power or pressure, frequency and duty (laser), gas and pressure, an optional ramp end value, and head motion during the pierce (none, wiggle or circular amplitude, or moving toward the path). Plasma uses one stage plus optional transfer height and puddle-jump (percent and dwell). Waterjet adds method, low-pressure value and abrasive delay.
- Pierce capacity per record: maximum pierceable thickness, and whether an edge start is allowed.
- Every number is entered by the user or copied from the maker's chart. Shipped example rows are marked "example" in the file and in the UI.

Editing: a cut-data table on the tool page (undoable commands, an MCP tool and script verb per the command law). The operation chooses a row (or "none: the machine's own table") and may override single values; overrides are commands too.

Operation behaviour: pierce at the start of the lead-in, run the stages in order (height move, dwell and head motion per stage), then the cut-height move and lead-in. The generated path carries the stages as records in the CL file so the post and the verifier read the same data.

Posts: each dialect writes the stages it can (dwell, height moves, selector codes or direct values). A stage or value the dialect cannot express makes the post refuse with a named reason, or write a visible comment line naming what was left to the control; it is never dropped silently. The Tormach post keeps M207/M208/M209 for the plasma values and refuses a multi-stage laser record.

## Safety rules

- A thickness above the tool's pierce capacity is refused, unless the operation states an edge start (then the lead-in must start off the plate, and that is verified).
- No silent default for a pierce time or height: an empty value either posts "controller's table" as an explicit, commented choice on a dialect that has one, or refuses.
- Stage values are checked at command creation (non-negative times and heights, power within 0 to 100 percent, at most four stages).
- Values are the user's and the machine maker's; shipped examples are labelled as examples and nothing was run on a real machine. Verification (stage order, pierce inside a kept part, head motion hitting a neighbour) joins the existing plasma laws.
- This changes posted output, so it is at least effort:high.

## Suggested slices

1. Tool-side cut-data record for the existing plasma torch (material and thickness rows, transfer height, puddle jump, pierce capacity), project file round-trip, undoable commands, MCP tool. The operation picks a row.
2. Plasma generation and the Tormach post use the row; refusal for thickness above capacity and the edge-start rule; laws and goldens.
3. Laser tool kind and machine kind with 1 to 4 pierce stages; CL records and a first laser post (dwell and height moves, explicit comment lines).
4. Waterjet tool kind: pierce methods, low-pressure pierce, abrasive delay; post support.
5. Docs and shipped example rows.

Slices 3 and 4 may need their own research issues for machine kinds; file them when slice 1 lands.

Done means: a plasma, laser or waterjet tool carries material and thickness keyed cut data with up to four ordered optional pierce stages; the operation uses the chosen row at the lead-in start; each post writes every stage or refuses or comments what it cannot; a too-thick plate without an edge start is refused; tests pin all of these.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: there are no operations for undercut cutters: T-slot, keyseat/woodruff, dovetail, lollipop. The cutter kinds themselves are open issue 896; this issue is the toolpath and its checks, and needs those kinds for its tools.

Wanted: a 2D "Slot undercut" family. The cutter enters outside the wall (or down a pre-cut slot wide enough for the neck), moves sideways into the undercut at depth, follows the slot or wall, and leaves the same way before any Z retract. Radial stepovers for cutters that cannot take the full width. For dovetail and lollipop the contact point is computed from the tool profile, not the tip.

Safety (why this is not a plain contour): a Z retract while the cutter head is under material is a crash. The op must refuse, by name, any link, retract or lead that lifts the head while its profile overlaps remaining stock above it. The stock simulation and the holder/shank checks must see the real profile (head wider than the neck), so the neck against the slot mouth is judged too.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on undercut and T-slot milling paths and on simulating non-convex tool profiles (tri-dexel or equivalent); the code is written from those and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: T-slot, keyseat and dovetail passes generate along a straight and a curved slot; a retract inside the undercut is refused in a test; simulation removes the undercut volume with the true profile; golden CL files; MCP tool; an entry slot too narrow for the neck is refused by name; the literature used is cited in the PR.

What is missing: there is no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth; it does not set depth from the width of the region.

Wanted: a 2D operation "V-carve" for V-bits (included angle from the tool). For closed regions (text, signs, inlays) the tool centre follows the medial axis and the depth at each point is the one where the cone touches both walls, limited by a maximum depth. Where the region is wider than the cone reaches at maximum depth, an optional flat-clearing pass (same or a second flat tool) removes the floor. Parameters are user choices with defaults: max depth, flat clearing on/off and its tool, start depth, stepdown for deep carves.

Safety: the cone must never cut outside the selected region at any depth (pinned by a test that sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline). A tool that is not a V-bit, an open region, or a tip flat larger than the narrowest feature is refused by name. Undoable command, MCP tool, simulation and collision checks like any 2D op.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published papers and handbooks on medial-axis / Voronoi-based V-carving; the algorithm is written from those and named in the module provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
